events.text: The White Stairs fall silent as the trap closes. The Jade Court's Rolls call you a Deep Stair immortal of modest standing, two rungs below the truth, and {npc} has built the whole corridor to that measure: wards cut for a lesser cultivator, {hn4_n} blades hung at exactly the right height. Nobody here has any idea what you have kept under the seal.

choices.text: Let the seal go, and let the corridor learn

effects.log: You loosen the seal one breath at a time, and the wards, cut to a smaller cultivator, begin to hum in protest.

choices.text: Fight as the rung they believe in

ok.log: You fight at the weight written in the Rolls, and it is somehow enough. {npc} has measured the wrong immortal.

fail.log: You hold the lesser rung too faithfully. The wards cut true, and it is a long way down the lower stair.

choices.text: Slip the wards and leave the isles by night

effects.log: You leave, the seal still whole. It is a clever exit and a lonely one.

events.text: A summons to the Ministry of Rites, and the doors close behind you with the soft sound of a well-kept lock. {npc} stands at the dais with {hn4_court} watching from the gallery. The roster says you are a minor sage of the Cloud Ranks; the dais has been laid with talismans for exactly that. It would be a very small trap for what you really are.

choices.text: Let the seal go, in front of the whole gallery

effects.log: The seal falls off in one piece, like a mask. In the gallery, a brush stops writing.

choices.text: Fight the trap as the minor sage they see

ok.log: You play the minor sage until the very last breath, then you do not. {npc} goes down with a look of honest professional grief.

fail.log: You are a minor sage a moment too long. The talismans bite, and you leave the dais on your knees.

choices.text: Bow to the gallery, and leave the Ministry unnoticed

effects.log: You bow and go. The gallery will remember a polite sage, and nothing else.

events.text: It is a supper on a cloud-barge, a courtesy between old rivals, and halfway between two isles the lamps go out. {hn4_n} shapes stand along the rail. The barge is warded against anything above the ranks written in the Rolls, and you are written two below your station. {npc} sets down the cup. It is, to be fair, a lovely cup.

choices.text: Let the seal go, over the water

effects.log: The seal slides away like a veil in the wind. The barge's wards creak, and the rail suddenly looks very thin.

choices.text: Fight on the deck as the lesser immortal you appear

ok.log: The deck is narrow and the lesser immortal is cunning. When the lamps relight, {npc} is sitting down who was not before.

fail.log: The wards are tuned to your false rung, and so are the blades. You go overboard with a gash in your side and no dignity.

choices.text: Drop to a passing skiff, and keep the seal

effects.log: You drop to a fisher's skiff and the barge sails on. Your secret rides with you, cold and unharmed.

events.text: The Court of Ascents has filed a writ, and the guard has come to your door with it. {npc} reads the charge in a clear voice. The guard are the Court's best, and every one of them is armed for a mere Sky-Gate immortal, which is what your seal tells the world you are. Behind them, two rungs up, a lot of careful planning is about to meet a surprise.

choices.text: Let the seal go on your own doorstep

effects.log: You let it go on your own step. The guard, who came for a Sky-Gate immortal, discover they are standing at the wrong door.

choices.text: Fight the writ-guard as a Sky-Gate immortal

ok.log: You fight them at the weight of a Sky-Gate immortal, and win by timing, which is the one thing nobody had written down.

fail.log: You keep to the false rung and the guard are better at it than you. They leave you bleeding on your own threshold.

choices.text: Take the writ as read, and leave before the hearing

effects.log: You leave with the seal intact, taking your sword and nothing else. The writ will have to find someone else to read it to.

events.text: The Book of Fates names you a Minor Warden of a Lesser Domain, two ranks below the truth, and {npc} has laid the trap in that exact measure: seven wards cut for a godling, offerings poisoned with a doubt, {hn4_n} voices waiting to call you thief. Nobody in the nave knows what is sealed behind your face.

choices.text: Let the seal go in the middle of the nave

effects.log: The seal lifts like incense smoke. The pillars of the nave, cut for a lesser god, begin to tremble.

choices.text: Fight as the Minor Warden the Book describes

ok.log: You fight at the weight the Book gave you, and it turns out to be exactly enough. {npc} measured the Book, not you.

fail.log: You hold to the lesser rank, and the wards, cut to that rank, hold you. You are cast out of the nave in pieces.

choices.text: Withdraw from the nave, and carry the seal into the star-road

effects.log: You step through a side door onto the star-road. The Book will never know it let you go.

events.text: A rite of Audit is called in your own temple, and a dozen heralds arrive to read your domain's accounts. {npc} is among them. The accounts say your altar draws a godling's share of faith, and the heralds have come armed for that. If they knew how much faith your seal is holding back, they would have come with more.

choices.text: Let the seal go in the middle of the Audit

effects.log: The accounts catch fire with sudden faith as the seal falls. A herald drops a ledger. Another sits down.

choices.text: Fight the heralds as the godling they audit

ok.log: You fight like the godling in the ledger, then, at the last breath, not like one. {npc} lowers a weapon that is, at this point, ornamental.

fail.log: The heralds take the godling's measure, and they are right to. You are carried out on a litter of other people's prayers.

choices.text: Close the temple quietly, and walk the star-road

effects.log: You close the ledgers, and the temple, and go. The Audit finds only a stack of books.

events.text: The trap is a feast of the lesser pantheons, set in a hall so old it has no roof. A hundred shrines send incense. Under every bowl, a thin ward, cut for a godling of low rank. {npc} lifts a cup. You could break the hall like a pane of glass; the hall, however, believes you could not.

choices.text: Let the seal go, and let the hall find out

effects.log: The seal falls into your cup like a coin. The incense changes direction, all at once, toward you.

choices.text: Fight your way out as the godling they invited

ok.log: You break the wards with a godling's tools, one at a time, patiently. {npc} watches the hall come apart in neat pieces.

fail.log: A godling's strength is a godling's strength. The wards tighten, and you leave the feast on a stretcher of smoke.

choices.text: Thank the host, and leave under the open sky

effects.log: You thank them for the hospitality and go. The hall believes it let a godling go. It was wrong, and happy to be.

events.text: A prayer-storm is turned on your altar by a rival pantheon, thousands of hostile whispers aimed at your name. {npc} stands at the storm's eye, and {hn4_court} watches. All of it is tuned to a god of the rank written in the Book. If you were that god, it would hurt a great deal. It is, in fact, a gift of wind to the sails of something larger.

choices.text: Let the seal go in the storm's eye

effects.log: The seal comes off and the prayer-storm, tuned to a lesser god, sags like a cloth in the rain.

choices.text: Fight the storm as the lesser god they believe in

ok.log: You answer the storm at the pitch of a lesser god, and the storm answers back too slowly. {npc} stumbles.

fail.log: The storm is tuned to the false rank and so is your fight. It breaks over you, and you are a long time finding the floor.

choices.text: Leave the altar to the storm, and go in silence

effects.log: You leave the altar to the storm. The storm is satisfied, and you are unseen, and the seal holds.

fail.log: The storm is tuned to the false rank and so is your fight. It breaks over you, and you are a long time finding the floor.

choices.text: Leave the altar to the storm, and go in silence

effects.log: You leave the altar to the storm. The storm is satisfied, and you are unseen, and the seal holds.

events.text: A prayer-storm is turned on your altar by a rival pantheon, thousands of hostile whispers aimed at your name. {npc} stands at the storm's eye, and {hn4_court} watches. All of it is tuned to a god of the rank written in the Book. If you were that god, it would hurt a great deal. It is, in fact, a gift of wind to the sails of something larger.

choices.text: Let the seal go in the storm's eye

effects.log: The seal comes off and the prayer-storm, tuned to a lesser god, sags like a cloth in the rain.

events.text: The summons from {hn4_court} is an honest one, on its face, and the hall is full of magistrates. The rolls say you are a middling talent of a quiet school, two ranks lower than the truth. {npc} has laid {hn4_n} guards and a ring of chalk for that measure. The chalk, you notice, is very fine chalk.

choices.text: Let the seal go, and watch the chalk

effects.log: The seal lifts like a cloth from a table. In the chalk ring, a line cracks.

choices.text: Fight the ring as the middling talent they see

ok.log: You are as middling as the rolls say, up to the last move, and then not. {npc} sits down in the chalk.

fail.log: You are too middling for the ring. The guards drive you to the floor, and a magistrate winces.

choices.text: Bow to the magistrates, and walk out of the kingdom

effects.log: You bow and walk. At the border post, the clerk stamps your papers without looking up.

events.text: A Warden of the League of Kingdoms arrives at your gate with a warrant, and {npc} walks beside {him}, very quiet, very sure. The warrant calls you a minor teacher of a minor school, and the Warden's escort was chosen for that. In the village, the children have stopped playing, and the dogs have lain down.

choices.text: Let the seal go, at your own gate

effects.log: You loosen it where you stand. The Warden's escort, chosen for a minor teacher, look at one another and take a step back.

choices.text: Fight the escort as the minor teacher they expect

ok.log: You fight at the weight in the warrant, and win by a hair, and a hair is what the Warden had not allowed for.

fail.log: The escort is chosen for exactly your weight, and it was a good choice. You wake in the village cart with a split lip.

choices.text: Take the back road out, with the seal still on

effects.log: You take the back road with your cloak pulled up. The Warden will find only a gate, a pot of tea, and cold ashes.

events.text: A Shadow Lodge has sold you out to the river-town magistrate, and the magistrate, in a rare burst of efficiency, has sent {hn4_n} constables to a warehouse by the quay to take you. {npc} keeps the keys. The warrant says you are a ferry-guild bodyguard of common rank, and the constables are armed for that. The warehouse smells of tar and rain.

choices.text: Let the seal go, among the tar-barrels

effects.log: The seal comes off with a small sound, like a coin on a tray. The nearest constable decides, with great speed, that duty lies elsewhere.

choices.text: Fight the constables as the ferry-bodyguard they know

ok.log: You fight as a hired guard, poorly, then well, in a way no hired guard has any right to. {npc} gives up the keys.

fail.log: You keep up the ferry-guard act, and the constables are good at ferry-guards. The tar is cold, and so is the floor.

choices.text: Slip out by the quay, and take the night boat

effects.log: You take the night boat in a hired hat. The river does not ask your name, and the seal stays on.

events.text: The school has called you home, they say, for a family matter, and in the courtyard where you learned your first form, {npc} waits with the elders and a bench of strangers. The elders remember you as a mid-ranked pupil, two ranks lower than you are. The courtyard is cleverly swept, so there are no loose stones to throw. It is a sad, careful ambush.

choices.text: Let the seal go, in the old courtyard

effects.log: The seal comes away on a long breath. An elder who taught you your first form sits down on the bench, rather suddenly.

choices.text: Fight as the mid-ranked pupil they remember

ok.log: You fight as the pupil they remember, and the courtyard gives you a pupil's room, and then you outgrow it. {npc} yields.

fail.log: They remember you too well. Every trick of the pupil is known, and the courtyard is swept clean of anything to lean on.

choices.text: Bow to your old teacher, and leave by the gate

effects.log: You bow to the elder who taught you, and leave. The courtyard has never been so polite.
